transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I’m here mostly because other people keep saying I’m doing too much. My family, some folks from church, even a couple of the younger guys at work—they act like I’ve got to slow down or let things wait. But the way I see it, things need doing, and somebody has to have the drive to get them done right.

We’re dealing with this move, and if I don’t stay on top of it, it’ll be boxes half-labeled and tools put where nobody can find them. Then there’s the new garage, which I don’t just want thrown together—I want it built right, solid, laid out so it actually works. And church has things that need organizing too, and I’ve always been someone people could count on there. Plus at work, these younger fellows, they mean well, but they don’t always know how the job ought to be done unless somebody shows them.

So I guess everyone thinks I’m taking on too much at once. To me it feels more like I’m the only one keeping up.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing more than usual?

Yes, I suppose there have been times like that. Lately especially, I just can’t seem to stay put. I’ll sit down in the chair thinking I’m going to rest for a minute, maybe drink some coffee or look over a list, and before I know it I’m back up again. It’s not even that I decide to get up exactly—my body just feels like it’s got a motor running in it.

I’ll start sorting boxes, then notice something needs measuring for the garage, then I’m loading tools or checking where something got packed, and then I’ll think, well, I’d better run back over to the old place because if I don’t, somebody’s going to forget something or put it in the wrong spot. I’m up and down constantly. Sitting more than a few minutes feels almost impossible, like I’m wasting time when there’s all this that needs doing.

Have there been times when you felt like you were on top of the world, better than everyone else, or that you could handle anything because you were just that capable? Or maybe you felt like people should listen to you because you knew more or could do things better than others?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t put it like I think I’m “better than everybody,” because that sounds arrogant, and I don’t like to think of myself that way. But I’ll tell you, lately I do feel like I can see what needs to happen clearer than everyone else. Like, if there’s a plan, then people ought to get behind it and stop picking at every little thing.

I’ll be in a real good mood sometimes, joking around, feeling like I’m ten feet tall, like there’s nothing we can’t get done if people would just move. And then my wife or my boy will ask me some little question—nothing terrible, just “Are you sure that’s where that should go?” or “Don’t you think we should wait?”—and I’ll just snap. Because to me it feels obvious, you know? Like, why are we slowing this down?

So yes, I guess I’ve been feeling like people need to either get on board with what I’m trying to do or get out of the way. Not because I’m trying to be mean, but because I feel like I know how to handle it, and when everybody starts second-guessing me, it just sets me off.
Have you noticed a decrease in how much sleep you need lately, like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep or not feeling tired even when you haven't slept much?

I don’t know that I’d say it that way, exactly. I mean, I haven’t sat down and counted the hours like that, you know? Some nights I’m up earlier than my wife thinks I ought to be, or I don’t settle down as quick because I’m thinking about what still needs doing, but I can’t say for sure, “Oh, I only need this much sleep now.”

I guess I just kind of go until I go. If there’s something that has to be handled, I’m not lying there wondering if I got the proper number of hours. I get up and do it. But as far as feeling rested after only a few hours or not needing sleep at all… I’m not sure. I haven’t really looked at it that way.
Over the past few weeks, have there been nights where you slept much less than usual but still felt fully energized the next day?

I’m not really sure, Doctor. I don’t want to give you an answer that sounds more definite than it is. I haven’t been keeping track of it that closely, like writing down when I went to bed and when I got up or anything.

There may have been nights where I slept less, sure, but whether it was “much less than usual” and then I felt fully energized the next day… I don’t know. I’ve just been getting up and doing what I feel needs doing. Sometimes I’m moving pretty early, and my wife might think I ought to still be resting, but in my mind I’m just thinking, well, there are things to handle.

So I can’t honestly say, “Yes, I only slept a few hours and felt great.” I haven’t noticed it in that clear a way. It’s more that I don’t pay as much attention to the sleep part when I’ve got things on my mind.
Have you had any nights recently where you slept a lot less than usual—like just a few hours—and then felt completely full of energy the next day without feeling tired?

I hear what you’re asking, and I know you’re trying to pin it down, but I honestly don’t have a clean yes-or-no for you. I can’t say, “Yes, Doctor, I slept just a few hours and then bounced up like nothing happened,” because I haven’t really been measuring it that way.

There’ve been nights where I know I didn’t settle down easy, or I was up earlier than maybe I normally would be, but whether it was only a few hours and then I felt completely full of energy… I’m just not sure. I don’t wake up and think, “Well, I got four hours, let’s see how I feel.” I just get moving if there’s something on my mind or something that needs doing.

My wife might have a better sense of whether I’m sleeping less, honestly, because she notices those things more than I do. From my side, I’d say I haven’t noticed some big clear pattern where I’m barely sleeping and not tired at all. It’s more that I don’t pay much attention to it when I’ve got things going through my head.
Have there been times in the past few weeks where you felt your mood was consistently higher than usual—like unusually upbeat, excited, or irritable—for several days in a row?

Yeah… that I can answer a little more clearly than the sleep thing. I have felt, I don’t know, more “up” or charged than normal at times, but it’s not just cheerful. It’s like I get this feeling that I know exactly what needs to happen, and everybody else needs to either get on board with what I’m trying to do or get out of my way.

And then it can flip on me. I’ll be joking around, feeling big, like I’m ten feet tall and everything I’m saying makes perfect sense, and then my wife or my boy will ask me some little question—nothing major, probably—and I’ll snap at them like they’re trying to block me or slow me down. Afterward I can see maybe I came on too strong, but in the moment it feels like, “Why are you questioning me? I’m trying to get things done here.”

So yes, I’d say over the past few weeks there have been stretches like that, where my mood’s been higher, or sharper, I guess—excited one minute and irritable the next. It’s not just a good mood. It’s got an edge to it.
Have you had any nights recently where you slept only a few hours and then felt completely full of energy the next day without feeling tired?

I know you’ve asked it a couple of times, and I’m not trying to be difficult, Doctor. I just don’t want to say yes to something if I’m not certain that’s what happened.

I can say I’ve had nights where I’m up later than I probably should be, or I wake up and my mind is already going, and I don’t really lie there thinking about being tired. I just get up and start doing whatever’s in my head. But whether that means I only slept “a few hours” and then felt completely full of energy the next day… I can’t honestly pin it down like that.

I don’t keep track of the clock very well. Sometimes I look at the time, sometimes I don’t. And if I’ve got something I’m focused on, I’m not sitting there checking, “Am I tired?” I’m more just moving. My wife might say, “You were up awfully early,” or something like that, but from my side it doesn’t register in a neat way.

So the most honest answer is: I’m not sure. I haven’t clearly noticed, “Oh, I slept only two or three hours and felt great.” It’s more blurry than that for me.
Over the past few weeks, has there been a time when your mood was clearly elevated or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four days in a row?

Yes, I think so. I mean, “elevated” sounds like a fancy word, but if you mean have I been running hotter than normal for days at a time—yeah. It’s not like I’m just happy or in a good mood. It’s more like I get this strong feeling that I know what the plan is, I know what needs to happen, and everybody around me needs to either get on board with me or get out of the way.

And it can last, yes. It’s not just five minutes and then gone. My wife would probably tell you I’ve been like that most of the day for stretches. I’ll be joking, talking big, feeling like I’m ten feet tall, like I’m making all the sense in the world, and then somebody—my wife or my boy—asks me some little question, and I take it like they’re challenging me. I’ll snap at them over nothing, really, because in that moment it feels like they’re slowing me down or getting in my way.

So yes, over the past few weeks there have been times like that for several days together. Excited, wound up, irritable… all mixed in.
Over the past few weeks, has there ever been a time when you felt this way—really high, irritable, or super charged—for a full week straight, without a break?

Yeah… I mean, if you’re asking whether it’s been just a couple of days here and there, no, it feels bigger than that. This whole thing has been going on for about a month now, really since we were forced to start leaving the old house.

That’s kind of the marker in my head. Before that, I don’t know, I had my moods like anybody else, but since all that started—packing, deciding what goes where, feeling pushed out of a place that was ours—I’ve felt charged up or on edge a lot of the time. I don’t know if I can neatly say “seven days straight with no break,” because I’m not sitting there with a calendar checking myself, but it hasn’t felt like one little spell and then I’m back to normal. It’s been this whole month-long thing, tied up with having to leave the house.

Before that, I don’t know, I had my moods like anybody else, but since all that started—packing, deciding what goes where, feeling pushed out of a place that was ours—I’ve felt charged up or on edge a lot of the time. I don’t know if I can neatly say “seven days straight with no break,” because I’m not sitting there with a calendar checking myself, but it hasn’t felt like one little spell and then I’m back to normal. It’s been this whole month-long thing, tied up with having to leave the house.
